translationRepairs: In the sixth month of summer, King Kuang of Lu's son, Marquis Min of Wuxiang, was installed as king.
In the sixth month of summer, King Qing of Lu's son, Marquis Min of Wuxiang, was installed as king.
魯頃王 uses the posthumous title 頃 (qǐng); Kuang invents a different title not present in the Chinese.
In the sixth month of summer, he established King Kuang of Lu's son Marquis Wuxiang Min as king.
In the sixth month of summer, he established King Qing of Lu's son Marquis Wuxiang Min as king.
The literal likewise misreads 頃 as Kuang; Qing correctly renders 魯頃王.

In the second month, the emperor enfeoffed the Imperial Grand Empress Dowager's younger cousin, Chamberlain Fu Shang, as Marquis of Ruchang, and the Empress Dowager's uterine younger brother, Chamberlain Zheng Ye, as Marquis of Yangxin.

In the second month, the emperor enfeoffed the Imperial Grand Empress Dowager's younger cousin, Chamberlain Fu Shang, as Marquis of Ruchang, and the son of the Empress Dowager's younger uterine brother, Chamberlain Zheng Ye, as Marquis of Yangxin.
太后同母弟子 identifies Zheng Ye as the son of the Empress Dowager's younger uterine brother; the revised wording restores 子 and states the relationship naturally in English.

In the third month, Chamberlain Dong Xian, Commandant of Equipage, Gentleman of the Interior Xi Fu Gong, and Governor Sun Chong of Nanyang were all enfeoffed as marquises for reporting on the King of Dongping.

In the third month, Chamberlain and Commandant of Equipage Dong Xian, Gentleman of the Interior Xi Fugong, and Governor Sun Chong of Nanyang were all enfeoffed as marquises for reporting on the King of Dongping.
侍中駙馬都尉董賢 assigns both offices to Dong Xian before the enumeration break; separating Commandant of Equipage invents a distinct office-holder, and Xi Fugong correctly treats 息夫 as the compound surname.

Guard General Dong Xian was appointed Grand Commandant; Chancellor Kong Guang became Grand Minister of Works; Chamberlain Peng Xuan became Grand Minister of Agriculture and was enfeoffed as Marquis of Changping.

Dong Xian, formerly Grand Commandant and General of the Guard, became Grand Commandant; Chancellor Kong Guang became Grand Minister over the Masses; Censor-in-Chief Peng Xuan became Grand Minister of Works and was enfeoffed as Marquis of Changping.
The title corrections match 大司徒, 御史大夫, and 大司空, while 'formerly' makes the apparent reform from Dong Xian's combined offices to Grand Commandant legible in English.

Grand Commandant Guard General Dong Xian became Grand Commandant, Chancellor Kong Guang became Grand Minister of Works, Chamberlain for the Palace Revenues Peng Xuan became Grand Minister of Agriculture, and was enfeoffed as Marquis of Changping.

Grand Commandant Guard General Dong Xian became Grand Commandant, Chancellor Kong Guang became Grand Minister over the Masses, Censor-in-Chief Peng Xuan became Grand Minister of Works, and was enfeoffed as Marquis of Changping.
The literal repeats the same office errors for 大司徒, 御史大夫, and 大司空; the proposed titles match the Chinese.

In the eighth month, an imperial edict declared: 'Previously I commanded Xia Helang and others to propose changing the reign title and extending the calendar periods, believing this would bring lasting stability to the nation.

In the eighth month, an imperial edict declared: 'Previously I commanded Xia Heliang and others to propose changing the reign title and extending the calendar periods, believing this would bring lasting stability to the nation.
夏賀良 is Hèliáng; Helang misreads 良 and should be Heliang.
